title: Measuring with units: end to end, no gaps
hook: Measuring with paper clips or blocks teaches what a unit is. The rules children learn here (same size, no gaps, no overlaps) are the same ones a ruler relies on.
coreIdeaMd:
Before rulers, children measure with **informal units**: blocks, paper clips, hand spans.

- Units must be the **same size**.
- Units go **end to end**, with no gaps and no overlaps.
- Start at one end of the object and stop at the other.

Comparing two objects directly (side by side, from the same starting line) comes first, then measuring with units.
workedExampleMd:
**Measuring a pencil with blocks.**

1. Line the first block up with the end of the pencil.
2. Place blocks end to end, touching, with no gaps.
3. Count the blocks: the pencil is 7 blocks long.

If the blocks are spread out with gaps, fewer blocks reach the end, so the answer comes out **too small**. Ask: "Why did two people get different answers for the same pencil?"

checkItems.stemMd: A student measures a book with paper clips but leaves gaps between the clips. What happens to their answer?
checkItems.feedbackCorrect: Yes. The gaps cover part of the length, so fewer clips are counted than are really needed.
checkItems.feedbackIncorrect: With gaps, each clip and its gap cover more of the book, so fewer clips get counted. The answer is too small.

wrongAnswers.feedback: The gaps are part of the length too, but nobody counts them. Fewer clips are counted than are needed to cover the book, so the answer is too small.

tryTomorrow: Ask two children to measure the same desk with blocks, one with gaps and one without. Compare the answers and ask the class to explain the difference.
reflectPrompt: What do your students do when two measurements of the same thing don't match?
